nodes.label: Auto-Edit Configuration Section
nodes.rationale: Master switch for LLM cut detection and editing; interactive mode stops at pending_review while auto applies when confident (threshold clamped to <= 0.99). fade_out_tail_seconds keeps extra source audio past the end cut so the delayed audio tail and the end fade clear the closing words.

nodes.label: Trash retention window
nodes.rationale: Defaults to 30 days and is overridable via SERMONPILOT_TRASH_RETENTION_DAYS or the trash_retention_days config key; item age is read from the item directory mtime.

nodes.label: trash_record.json audit record
nodes.rationale: The record is the audit trail for a restore; a failed move leaves the source alone and returns a record with moved=false.

nodes.label: Cut detection
nodes.rationale: Automatic application requires a healthy detection result, sufficient confidence, and a valid plan; otherwise the result is surfaced as a failure for review.

nodes.label: Deterministic sermon record
nodes.rationale: Re-runs, re-renders, and refine loops update one record and preserve its history instead of creating a second Library row.

nodes.label: Job worker
nodes.rationale: The worker currently initializes inside the legacy Streamlit process and the API bridge only submits jobs, so console-submitted jobs wait until the legacy interface is opened once after a restart.

nodes.label: Legacy Streamlit interface
nodes.rationale: Retained on its own port; its retirement is a separate decision.

nodes.label: Dated trash area for media deletion
nodes.norm_label: dated trash area for media deletion
nodes.rationale: Media deletion is recoverable: local files move into a dated trash area with a record of original and new locations, while cloud objects stay on their remote unless a remote change is required.

nodes.label: Browser console
nodes.rationale: The console keeps actions aligned with the record's review state and refuses to publish a sermon awaiting review, so the raw source is never uploaded by accident.

nodes.label: Embeddings and RAG Removal
nodes.rationale: Owner decision to remove the feature in full; no console section to map to because the surface is gone, not deferred.

nodes.label: Environment Override Display
nodes.rationale: Visible form of the rule that the environment always overrides saved settings: a field shows a badge naming the variable, db/default show none.

nodes.label: Per-user Upload Routing
nodes.rationale: Credentials resolve at job-execution time from the owning user's connections.sermonaudio setting and the job config is rebound before the engine runs, so a job can never publish as another user; console refuses before queueing and the executor refuses as second line of defence.

nodes.label: Cancellation Documentation
nodes.rationale: A hook only helps if the code holding the worker gets a chance to run it; a blocking subprocess.run does not, which is why external commands run through supervised polling children.

nodes.label: SermonPilot 1.8.0
nodes.rationale: Moves more of the operator workflow into the browser console while keeping the processing engine and the legacy interface available.

nodes.label: save_sermon()
nodes.rationale: Only writes content columns that are supplied, so a metadata-only run cannot blank a stored description or hashtags.

nodes.label: POST /api/sermons/{id}/metadata/generate
nodes.rationale: Runs on the request thread with a 300-second wall-clock bound and persists the value before returning so a later Generate & Upload reads it from the row; generation reads only the edit plan's kept ranges so material the render drops is never sent to the model.

nodes.label: POST /api/sermons/{id}/description/regenerate
nodes.rationale: Queues a metadata_update job through the normal job queue instead of regenerating synchronously, and returns 409 when another job for the sermon is already active.

nodes.label: llm_manager.chat()
nodes.rationale: Tries the provider chain: primary, then the configured fallbacks.

nodes.label: DescriptionGenerationError
nodes.rationale: Carries provider, elapsed_seconds, and attempts so the caller can log the real cause.

nodes.label: generate_summary()
nodes.rationale: Either returns usable prose or raises; previously it returned the literal string 'Summary generation failed' and callers stored it, so failure text landed in sermons.description and read as a success in the logs.

nodes.label: generate_validated_summary()
nodes.rationale: Returns description plus validation_info whose final_status is no_validation, approved_primary, approved_fallback, or needs_review.

nodes.label: sermons.description_needs_review flag
nodes.rationale: An integer column added by the idempotent startup migration; a failed generation sets it to 1 and a successful generation clears it to 0.

nodes.label: Configurable validation criteria
nodes.rationale: Default criteria focus on theological content, speaker message, professional style, substance over generic phrases, and practical application, and are configurable per organization.

nodes.label: llm.validator configuration
nodes.rationale: A smaller, faster model is used for validation; regeneration_threshold, min/max length thresholds, and criteria are configurable under metadata_processing.description.validation.

nodes.label: SermonDatabase.init_database
nodes.rationale: Runs dedupe and owner repair at end; read-only subclass does not run it so a read-only connection never writes.

nodes.label: repair_ownerless_sermons
nodes.rationale: Reads sermon_publish background_jobs to assign owner only when exactly one job names a NULL-owned sermon; only touches NULL owners so a second run changes nothing.

nodes.label: SermonRepository.dedupe_sermons
nodes.rationale: Groups by identity_key (speaker/date/title without fingerprint) so a draft from a re-staged file folds into its earlier row; idempotent by construction.

nodes.label: _fold_sermon
nodes.rationale: Folds loser into survivor; never replaces a recorded file path, longest value wins per content field, and a processed loser promotes the survivor so a published sermon is never downgraded.

nodes.label: _identity_score
nodes.rationale: Orders survivor selection: existing media, remote id, processed/draft status, highest revision, transcript length, then notes; ties broken by revision, updated_at, then id.

nodes.label: SermonRepository.save_sermon
nodes.rationale: Upserts on primary key, refreshing sermon columns but leaving edit_plans, notes and sermon_content untouched so re-runs keep history; sets user_id only when NULL so first creator keeps ownership.

nodes.label: Sermon Identity
nodes.rationale: Identity is normalised speaker, recorded date and title plus a source-media fingerprint; the database never holds two rows for one sermon and identity ignores user_id.

nodes.label: Identity and User Ownership
nodes.rationale: Identity ignores user_id so two users submitting the same attributes resolve to one row; first creator keeps ownership and an ownerless legacy row stays admin-only until repaired.

nodes.label: Source Media Fingerprint
nodes.rationale: Samples size plus first and last MiB rather than full hashing: full hashing of multi-gigabyte recordings per request would cost more than the duplicate it prevents, and size plus both ends make accidental matches impractical.

nodes.label: .env.example
nodes.rationale: Environment variables keep precedence over stored settings for each running process, so rotating a key in .env and restarting is enough.

nodes.label: GET /api/health
nodes.rationale: The checked-in compose file disables the container healthcheck (test: ["NONE"]), so this public request is the health check.

nodes.label: web/dist built bundle
nodes.rationale: The API serves the built bundle from web/dist inside the image, so a blank console usually means the bundle is missing or stale.

nodes.label: ghcr.io/barbelldwarf/sermonpilot image
nodes.rationale: Release tags carry a backend suffix (cuda/rocm/cpu) so the operator can pick the build matching the host GPU; latest points at the latest CUDA build.

nodes.label: Container ports 8504 / 8501
nodes.rationale: The checked-in compose file publishes only 8501, so a plain compose up exposes the legacy UI until the 8504 mapping is added.

nodes.label: config/config.example.yaml
nodes.rationale: Settings load from the SQLite settings database seeded from environment variables on first run; no file is read at run time. This file is a reference showing every recognized key; a pre-database config.yaml (or the file named by SA_UPDATER_CONFIG) is imported into an empty database once.

nodes.label: docker-compose.yml
nodes.rationale: Defines a single sermon-pilot service; no separate API, Redis, PostgreSQL, or Ollama container — Ollama runs outside the container via OLLAMA_HOST.

nodes.label: docker-compose.gpu.yml
nodes.rationale: Override file that adds NVIDIA device reservations for GPU compute.

nodes.label: docker/start_production.sh
nodes.rationale: Entrypoint creates persistent directories, repairs ownership, initializes SQLite, starts job worker, Streamlit, and optional web API.

nodes.label: credential-scan job
nodes.rationale: Trufflehog's BASE/HEAD scan needs two distinct commits; on pushes to master (base == head) it errors out, so the scan runs only on pull requests.

nodes.label: dependency-security job
nodes.rationale: Audits the authoritative dev lock and also the production resolution compiled from the requirements floors, matching how Docker installs dependencies.

nodes.label: security-scan job
nodes.rationale: config.yaml is untracked (runtime artifact); the committed example is validated because it is the artifact contributors actually change.

nodes.label: ui/requirements-ui.txt
nodes.rationale: UI-specific dependencies are kept separate from the core project requirements.

nodes.label: Bandit
nodes.rationale: -lll fails the job on HIGH severity findings only; pre-existing MEDIUM/LOW findings are reported in the artifact.

nodes.label: config.example.yaml (Canonical Config)
nodes.rationale: The example config remains canonical; variant templates may drift except for the variant-specific transcription section.

nodes.label: Enhancement Compute Placement (auto/cpu/cuda)
nodes.rationale: auto runs DeepFilterNet on CPU when total VRAM is below min_gpu_vram_gb so whisper keeps the card; cuda needs room for enhancement and whisper together.

nodes.label: GPU Build Backends (cpu/cuda/rocm)
nodes.rationale: GPU_BACKEND build arg selects image flavor; cuda installs onnxruntime-gpu, rocm installs requirements-rocm.txt.

nodes.label: Headless Job Worker
nodes.rationale: Worker starts by default and logs 'worker started, owns lease' when it owns the queue lease; SERMONPILOT_JOB_WORKER_ENABLED=0 enables submit-only deployments.

nodes.label: LLM Providers (ollama/openai/xai/groq/openrouter)
nodes.rationale: Fallback LLM is used if the primary fails; a smaller validator model performs description validation.

nodes.label: API-Key Environment Placeholder Contract
nodes.rationale: Never store literal keys; every api_key is a ${VAR} placeholder resolved from the environment at load time. A key may also come from the UI-saved DB config_cache; precedence is environment > DB > built-in default, and the Settings UI YAML export writes placeholders, never literals.

nodes.label: Enhancement Compute Placement
nodes.rationale: auto runs DeepFilterNet on CPU when the GPU's total VRAM is below min_gpu_vram_gb so whisper keeps the card; cpu always leaves the GPU free for transcription; cuda is fastest but needs room for enhancement and whisper together. preprocess_noise_gate is kept false because it destroyed sermon speech.

nodes.label: Ingest Watcher Configuration Section
nodes.rationale: Default off so existing deployments are unchanged; Docker launches the watcher only when INGEST_WATCHER_ENABLED is truthy, so setting enabled: true alone does not start it inside the container. With Signal sender/recipients unset the watcher logs 'notify disabled' and only records detections.

nodes.label: Job Queue Configuration Section
nodes.rationale: A queued job starts only when the host has free RAM and GPU VRAM resources above the configured floors.

nodes.label: LLM Configuration Section
nodes.rationale: Fallback settings are used if the primary LLM fails; the validator is a smaller, faster model used for description validation; optional operation-scoped pins (e.g. auto_edit) fall back to the global primary/fallback chain when absent.

nodes.label: Transcription Configuration Section
nodes.rationale: Backend precedence: an explicit value always wins; auto picks faster_whisper_local when the optional faster-whisper (CTranslate2) package is importable (lighter, lower VRAM), otherwise whisper_local (fp16 on CUDA, drops to CPU on CUDA OOM). compute_type auto = int8 on cpu, float16 on cuda because an 8 GB card cannot hold a float32 large model; cuda loads still step down the ladder on OOM.

nodes.label: Anthropic Claude via OpenAI-Compatible Proxy
nodes.rationale: src/llm_manager.py has no native Anthropic provider; base_url must point at an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (proxy/gateway), not api.anthropic.com directly.

nodes.label: xAI Grok Primary with OpenAI Fallback
nodes.norm_label: xai grok primary with openai fallback
nodes.rationale: xAI Grok is reached through the OpenAI-compatible provider by setting base_url to https://api.x.ai/v1.

nodes.label: Settings Resolution Precedence
nodes.rationale: Precedence is built-in defaults, then per-variant template (fresh database only), then the SQLite config_cache.app_config row, then environment variables mapped in src/core/config.py::ENV_CONFIG_MAP. Environment variables always win while set; deploy-time secrets (API keys) stay in the environment and are never copied into the database.

nodes.label: Per-Variant Template Import
nodes.rationale: The Dockerfile sets SERMONPILOT_VARIANT and the matching template is imported into the settings database once, on a fresh database only; after that the database is authoritative.

nodes.label: CPU Variant Transcription Settings
nodes.rationale: CPU-only image, so both local backends use device cpu with int8 compute; CTranslate2 int8 is the fastest accurate option on CPU.

nodes.label: Ollama
nodes.rationale: Local LLM alternative to cloud API providers, available when no API key is configured.

nodes.label: SERMONPILOT_RAW_INGEST input boundary
nodes.rationale: Raw ingest is an input boundary only; it cannot become a user output or file-browsing root, and path resolution is restricted to the requesting user's own subdirectory so sibling uploads and .. traversal are rejected.

nodes.label: Settings DB config_cache
nodes.rationale: SQLite settings survive restarts and are what the web UI Settings page edits; env vars seed it once on first launch and UI-saved keys live here, masked as ${VAR} on YAML export.

nodes.label: LLM Provider Examples
nodes.rationale: EXAMPLE FILE ONLY - DO NOT USE IN PRODUCTION; use as overlays via SA_UPDATER_CONFIG or copy a section into the UI config import. Keys must match what src/llm_manager.py reads.

nodes.label: Configuration Directory README
nodes.rationale: No file in the configuration directory is read at run time; the directory holds Docker-shipped templates plus YAML examples kept for reference.

nodes.label: CPU Image Variant Template
nodes.rationale: CPU-only build (no GPU wheels); both local transcription backends run on CPU, and int8 is the fast, memory-light choice.

nodes.label: CUDA Config Template
nodes.rationale: CUDA image variant: both local transcription backends run on the GPU with float16 compute, falling back to CPU automatically when torch cannot see a CUDA device.

nodes.label: ROCm Config Template
nodes.rationale: ROCm image variant: torch-based whisper_local uses the AMD GPU via HIP through the CUDA device interface, while faster-whisper is pinned to CPU int8 because CTranslate2 has no ROCm support and would raise CUDA driver version errors.

nodes.label: Build and Push Docker Images Workflow
nodes.norm_label: build and push docker images workflow
nodes.rationale: Actions are pinned to commit SHAs of their release tags to prevent supply-chain tampering; the tag is noted in a trailing comment.

nodes.label: tag-latest job
nodes.rationale: Retags the cuda image as latest on v-tag builds.

nodes.label: Release Workflow
nodes.rationale: Releases are cut by CI so a merged version bump can never ship untagged; token-pushed refs fire no push events, so the tag job also drafts the release and dispatches the docker build.

nodes.label: create-release-tag job
nodes.rationale: Token-pushed refs fire no push events, so this job also drafts the release and dispatches the docker build from the tag ref.

nodes.label: draft-github-release job
nodes.rationale: Runs on manual tag pushes: validates the tag against pyproject.toml, then drafts the GitHub Release with auto-generated notes unless a draft already exists.

nodes.label: release-version-check job
nodes.rationale: Fails a release PR unless the pyproject.toml version is a valid MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH bump above the latest tag, is not tagged yet, and matches the release branch name.

nodes.label: Clear Enhancement (clear-studio / clear-natural)
nodes.rationale: ONNX model variant follows the method name (clear-natural loads clear-natural.onnx, clear-studio loads clear-studio.onnx); can be skipped entirely with method none.

nodes.label: DeepFilterNet Audio Enhancement
nodes.rationale: Runs on PyTorch and uses CUDA when torch.cuda.is_available() is true, with automatic ROCm detection via torch.version.hip; generally uses more memory than Clear ONNX inference.

nodes.label: ONNX Runtime
nodes.rationale: Supports CUDA and CPU; on ROCm 7.x it runs on CPU because published onnxruntime-rocm wheels are built against the ROCm 6.4.2 ABI and are incompatible with 7.x, which is still fast enough for sermon-length audio.

nodes.label: PyTorch (torch / torchaudio)
nodes.rationale: Pinned once at torch>=2.13.0 / torchaudio>=2.11.0; every install must satisfy that floor. torchaudio 2.11.0 is its final upstream release, trails torch on every index, and its wheels declare no torch dependency, so the documented pairs are the tested ones.

nodes.label: AMD ROCm
nodes.rationale: ROCm exposes HIP through the CUDA device interface, which is why torch-based components work on AMD GPUs.

nodes.label: whisper_local (openai-whisper)
nodes.rationale: Runs on torch, so it uses NVIDIA CUDA and AMD ROCm GPUs; preferred backend on AMD hardware.

nodes.label: faster_whisper_local
nodes.rationale: CTranslate2 has no ROCm support, so _detect_device(allow_rocm=False) forces it to CPU (int8) on AMD GPUs instead of failing with 'CUDA driver version is insufficient'.

nodes.label: Upload Existing Render
nodes.rationale: Exists because both approve buttons re-render; when a render already exists the operator wants the upload and nothing else.

nodes.label: ENV_CONFIG_MAP
nodes.rationale: Environment variables mapped here take precedence over the SQLite config row and built-in defaults.

nodes.label: Upload Only Mode
nodes.rationale: Reuses the stored render and skips the pipeline so the operator gets the upload without re-running enhancement, cut detection or encode.

nodes.label: Button primitive (Button, buttonClass)
nodes.rationale: Only one primary per view so the primary path stays unambiguous; secondary actions belong in a Menu.

nodes.label: Chip primitive (24px status pill)
nodes.rationale: Chips are state-only and not clickable, so status colouring never becomes decoration.

nodes.label: Input and select controls
nodes.rationale: Labels are always visible; placeholders are examples, never labels.

nodes.label: Menu primitive
nodes.rationale: Menus are for overflow, not the primary path; primitive handles arrow keys, Home/End, Escape, focus return and outside click.

nodes.label: Switch and Toggle controls
nodes.rationale: Switch is used where the label lives in the surrounding row, Toggle where the control itself is the row.

nodes.label: Toast system (useToast, ToastHost)
nodes.rationale: Hover and focus pause timers and destructive actions offer Undo so users can recover from an accidental confirm.

nodes.label: FastAPI bridge (server/api, port 8504)
nodes.rationale: Serves the live bundle plus /api/* so the eventual front-door cutover is a one-line nginx upstream move.

nodes.label: P5f Files API scoping decision
nodes.rationale: Until per-user output dirs fully land, the configured output directory IS the user boundary; path traversal blocked via resolve + prefix check.

nodes.label: Front-door cutover (P6c, prepared not switched)
nodes.rationale: Cutover is a manual two-step operator action (flip web_console_ready, move nginx upstream 8501->8504) with a one-line rollback; nothing in the repo switches traffic on its own.

nodes.label: Live mode (VITE_API_MODE=live, FastAPI bridge)
nodes.rationale: App builds twice from the same source so mode is baked in at build time rather than branched in code.

nodes.label: Media streaming API (range previews)
nodes.rationale: Paths come only from sermon_files/metadata.json and must resolve under allowed dirs, so a tampered row cannot read arbitrary files; media tags cannot send Authorization headers, hence ?token= accepted on these routes only.

nodes.label: Mock mode (VITE_API_MODE=mock)
nodes.rationale: Default build mode so the console is demonstrable without a backend; local-only actions confirm with (mock) toasts.

nodes.label: Per-user ownership model (P5b)
nodes.rationale: NULL user_id means unowned/legacy and stays admin-visible; foreign single-row fetches return 404 rather than 403 so resource existence is not leaked. Columns are added by PRAGMA-checked _ensure_columns because CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS never alters existing tables.

nodes.label: Console phase plan (1-3)
nodes.rationale: Phase 1 is scaffold/tokens/shell with mock data so screens exist before real routing and backend wiring in Phase 2.

nodes.label: Release readiness v1.7.0 console scope (P7)
nodes.rationale: Batch update, validation, import pages, resume-upload, cloud mounts and overlay cards are deliberately parked so v1.7.0 ships the end-to-end New Sermon path.

nodes.label: Roadmap: per-user cloud storage mounts
nodes.rationale: Each user gets a separate rclone configuration so the New Sermon picker can browse a connected remote; shipped in v1.8.0.

nodes.label: Roadmap: resumable/interruptible uploads
nodes.rationale: Server-side chunk-offset session lets large browser uploads pause/resume across browser restart, network drop or reboot; not started until the write-path phase lands.

nodes.norm_label: roadmap: scripture overlay + audio disclaimer intro

nodes.label: Colour role tokens (ink/surface/accent/status)
nodes.rationale: Status semantics are fixed (ok=done, warn=waiting for a person, danger=failed, info=running/applied, neutral=draft/unknown); a chip never changes tone for decoration.

nodes.label: Motion rules (140-200ms, reduced-motion)
nodes.rationale: Essential information must never be hidden behind motion; reduced-motion removes shimmer, sheet, menu and stagger animation.

nodes.label: Type scale and font roles

nodes.label: CI Workflow
nodes.rationale: Actions are pinned to commit SHAs of their release tags to prevent supply-chain tampering.

nodes.label: Run Fast Tests Step (pytest -m 'not heavy')
nodes.rationale: The fast suite imports only lightweight packages, so the full requirements set (torch, whisper, ...) stays out of CI.

nodes.label: Build Web Bundle / Test Web Components Step
nodes.norm_label: build web bundle / test web components step
nodes.rationale: The SPA tests need web/dist, so the web bundle is built before running them.

nodes.label: Hardware Variant Config Templates (cuda/rocm/cpu.yaml)
nodes.rationale: Templates differ only in the transcription section (backend, device, compute type) matched to the image's hardware stack; runtime config lives in the settings DB and config.yaml is optional (export/import only).

nodes.label: Configuration-Driven Everything
nodes.rationale: Resolution order is defaults, optional per-variant template, database, env overrides, then ${VAR} substitution, so the settings DB is the single source of truth and no config file is required; a legacy config.yaml is imported once.

nodes.label: Dual-Provider Pattern (LLM + Audio)
nodes.rationale: LLM uses primary/fallback/validator providers and audio uses enhancement-method-with-no-op-fallback so a single unavailable backend does not break the pipeline.

nodes.label: Graceful Degradation Chain
nodes.rationale: Processing should complete rather than fail: audio falls back to copying the original file, LLM falls through primary to fallback provider, and models fall back from GPU (CUDA/ROCm) to CPU.

nodes.label: pytest 'heavy' Test Marker
nodes.rationale: Default pytest run stays an offline fast suite; tests needing network, audio, or GPU are marked heavy and skipped unless --run-heavy is passed.

nodes.label: Linux platform requirements
nodes.rationale: Uses the PyTorch CUDA (cu121) extra index so Linux installs get GPU support; defers GPU and AI-model extras to optional include files so the base install stays CPU-only.

nodes.label: DeepFilterNet model requirements (Linux)
nodes.rationale: Isolated into its own file so the heavy DeepFilterNet/Torch model stack is only installed when denoising is wanted; Torch floor kept identical to pyproject.

nodes.label: requirements.txt
nodes.rationale: Derived mirror of the [project] dependencies block, regenerated with uv export, so the Dockerfile and wheel install the same set.

nodes.label: requirements-dev.txt
nodes.rationale: Mirror of the [dev] extra in pyproject.toml; keeps optional dev tooling out of the base runtime install.

nodes.label: requirements-gpu.txt
nodes.rationale: Overrides the torch family from requirements.txt with CUDA 12.6 builds via the PyTorch extra index.

nodes.label: torch (CUDA 12.6 build)
nodes.rationale: Single pin per index with the same floor as pyproject.toml.

nodes.label: torchaudio (CUDA 12.6 build)
nodes.rationale: torchaudio's final upstream release is 2.11.0 and declares no torch dependency; the pair is verified against torch 2.14 for GPU resample and DeepFilterNet enhancement.

nodes.label: deepfilternet
nodes.rationale: Must be imported in code as 'df', not as 'deepfilternet'.

nodes.label: torch (CPU/default build)
nodes.rationale: Single pin with the same floor as pyproject.toml; GPU variants override it via the commented cu126 pins.

nodes.label: requirements-rocm.txt
nodes.rationale: onnxruntime-rocm wheels are built against ROCm 6.4.2 ABI (libhipblas.so.2, libamdhip64.so.6, hipblasGemmStridedBatchedEx_v2) and are incompatible with ROCm 7.x; ONNX inference therefore runs on CPU (~10x realtime, fast enough for sermon-length audio) while PyTorch operations (DeepFilterNet DSP) do use the GPU. ORT GPU on ROCm would require installing ROCm 6.4.2 and rebuilding onnxruntime from source.

nodes.label: torch (ROCm 7.1 build)
nodes.rationale: torch and torchaudio are released independently on ROCm, so each is pinned per-index.

nodes.label: torchaudio (ROCm 7.1 build)
nodes.rationale: torch and torchaudio are released independently on ROCm, so each is pinned per-index.

nodes.label: DeepFilterNet model requirements (Windows)
nodes.rationale: Windows mirror of the Linux DeepFilterNet file so the model stack is installed per-platform; Torch floor kept identical to pyproject.

nodes.label: Windows platform requirements
nodes.rationale: Uses the PyTorch CUDA (cu126) extra index for Windows GPU support and mirrors pyproject base deps rather than re-declaring them.

nodes.label: Derived Mirror
nodes.rationale: requirements.txt is generated from pyproject.toml rather than hand-maintained, keeping one authoritative dependency declaration.

nodes.label: PyTorch Index Overrides
nodes.rationale: Torch family pinned once in pyproject.toml; per-index override files add the matching index and pin the same version with the platform suffix.

nodes.label: UV
nodes.rationale: Fast Python package and version manager; drop-in pip replacement that also manages Python versions, reducing the need for pyenv.

nodes.label: Linux-Specific Requirements
nodes.rationale: Linux installs must use --index-strategy unsafe-best-match so the PyTorch CUDA index can be used alongside PyPI.

nodes.label: All AI Enhancement Models Requirements
nodes.rationale: Some models may have conflicting dependencies, so they are optional/commented and installed individually if needed.

nodes.label: PerformanceMonitor.get_processing_metrics()
nodes.rationale: When the database or its tables are missing the method returns zeroed values rather than raising, so the monitor degrades gracefully.

nodes.label: PerformanceMonitor.get_system_metrics()
nodes.rationale: GPU metrics come from nvidia-smi; if that fails the monitor falls back to torch.cuda detection, which reports only the device name and total memory.
